content: This medication, sulfasalazine, is used to manage ulcerative colitis, a specific type of bowel disease. While it does not cure the condition, it helps alleviate symptoms such as fever, abdominal pain, diarrhea, and rectal bleeding. After an acute episode is treated, sulfasalazine is also prescribed to prolong the time between attacks. Additionally, the delayed-release form of sulfasalazine is used to treat rheumatoid arthritis by reducing joint pain, swelling, and stiffness. Early treatment of rheumatoid arthritis with sulfasalazine can help prevent or minimize further joint damage, enabling patients to maintain their daily activities. To use this medication, take it orally after meals with a full glass of water (8 ounces or 240 milliliters) as directed by your doctor. To reduce the risk of stomach upset, your doctor may recommend gradually increasing the dosage when starting treatment. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. If you are taking the delayed-release tablets, swallow them whole without crushing, chewing, or breaking them. It is important to stay hydrated during treatment unless otherwise instructed by your doctor. Take this medication consistently to achieve the best results. Inform your doctor if your condition does not improve or worsens. Common side effects may include stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, headache, dizziness, or unusual fatigue. This medication may also cause your skin and urine to turn an orange-yellow color. Rarely, delayed-release tablets may appear whole or partially dissolved in your stool. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. However, serious side effects, such as severe allergic reactions (e.g., Stevens-Johnson syndrome), blood disorders (e.g., agranulocytosis, aplastic anemia), liver damage, nerve or muscle problems, and infections, may occur in rare cases. If you experience any severe symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Before taking sulfasalazine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, sulfa drugs, aspirin, related drugs (e.g., salicylates, NSAIDs like ibuprofen), mesalamine, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Sulfasalazine may cause dizziness, and consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can worsen this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. Sulfasalazine is similar to aspirin and may temporarily affect male fertility. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. Caution is advised if it is used near the expected delivery date, as similar drugs may harm a newborn. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately. Sulfasalazine may lower folic acid levels, increasing the risk of spinal cord defects. This drug passes into breast milk and may have undesirable effects on a nursing infant. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Sulfasalazine is very similar to mesalamine and may interfere with certain lab tests (e.g., urine normetanephrine levels, liver function tests), potentially causing false results. In case of an overdose with serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Regular lab and medical tests (e.g., complete blood count, liver and kidney function) should be conducted while taking this medication. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
